This section provides access to **interactive Jupyter notebooks** powered by Binder.

Binder creates a temporary, cloud-based Jupyter environment so you can run and explore notebooks without installing anything locally. This is intended for deeper, more involved content where full Python packages are required.

## <i class="fa-regular fa-circle-play" aria-hidden="true"></i> [Launch Binder session to start running notebooks in minutes!](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/pixel-process-dev/pixel-process/binder)

<hr class="page-divider">

::: {.callout icon="none" .custom-callout .experiment title="Binder is a Powerful Learning Tool"}

Environment setup can cause friction when learning from or sharing your own notebooks. Binder offers a free way to streamline the process by providing a minimial, temporary, hassle-free approach to running notebooks. By using preset environments and package details, rapid exploration, testing, and sharing is possible with minimal complications.
:::


## Binder Basics

<div class="category-grid">
<div class="category-card">
<h3>Startup Time</h3>
<ul>
<li>Initial startup may take **1-3 minutes**</li>
<li>Subsequent launches are often faster due to caching</li>
<li>Please be patient while the environment is prepared</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="category-card">
<h3>Sessions are Temporary</h3>
<ul>
<li>Sessions are **ephemeral**</li>
<li>Files or changes you make **will be lost** when the session ends</li>
<li>Download or copy code elsewhere to save work</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="category-card">
<h3>Multiple Notebooks Allowed</h3>
<ul>
<li>You can open and run **any notebook in this directory**</li>
<li>You can explore multiple notebooks in the **same session**</li>
<li>Outputs, variables, and files persist **within the active session**</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="category-card">
<h3>Minimal Environment</h3>
<ul>
<li>Binder provides a clean, minimal Jupyter environment</li>
<li>No custom UI extensions or settings stored</li>
<li>Appearance and features may differ from a local Jupyter Lab setup</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

<hr class="page-divider">

## Binder Quickstart

1. Wait for Binder to finish starting
2. Open a notebook from the file browser
3. Run cells as instructed in the notebook
4. Explore freely, knowing the session is temporary

<hr class="page-divider">
